body.estimand_functional: \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{sel}}=\widehat\tau_{\widehat J},\quad C_z(k)=\int_{-\infty}^{k}\phi(x)g_{\rho_1}(x;z)\,dx+\int_k^{\infty}\phi(x)g_{\rho_2}(x;z)\,dx,\quad T_{\mathrm{gap}}=(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{gap}}-\tau)/\widehat{\operatorname{se}}_{\widehat J_A}\), with uniform selector-conditional standard-normal approximation for the last statistic on \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{stab}}(D_{\mathrm{gap}})\) only.

sampling_model.design: Observational long-panel sampling with two predeclared square donor/proxy partitions and deterministic treatment onset after period \(n\).
sampling_model.units: One treated unit and a fixed-dimensional vector of untreated controls observed for \(n+m\) periods.
sampling_model.treatment: The treated outcome equals \(Y_t(0)\) before onset and \(Y_t(0)+\Delta_t\) afterward; controls remain untreated.
sampling_model.overlap: Not applicable; identification is through two valid proximal bridge systems with fixed singular-value margin.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The conventional procedure uses all pre-period observations both to select and fit. The corrected procedure selects on the first \(\lfloor\varrho n\rfloor\) observations, discards \(\lceil(\log n)^2\rceil\), estimates \(\widehat M_{B,s}\) and \(\widehat\alpha_{B,s}\) on the late block, estimates \(\widehat\mu_{C,s}\) on the post block, forms \(\widehat H_{B,C,s}\), and computes separate future-only fitted pre and post scores. Bartlett estimates with \(h_n=\lfloor\min(N_{B,n},m)^{1/5}\rfloor\) are scaled by \(N_{B,n}^{-1}\) and \(m^{-1}\); every inverse and nonpositive-variance case has a fixed measurable fallback.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Predetermined square donor and supplemental-proxy roles support fixed-role proximal identification and inference under the published structural conditions.
Local post-model-selection sequences exhibit nonregularity and obstruct uniform approximations.
Adaptive proximal procedures select among potentially invalid proxy specifications, a different selection target from exchanging two valid donor/proxy roles.
Simultaneous protection across candidate models gives post-selection coverage under arbitrary selection rules rather than exact ordinary-Wald validity.
Gaussian half-space conditioning yields a truncated-normal selective pivot.
Explicit Gaussian formulas describe coverage after selection between nested regressions.
Even Gaussian functionals have a symmetry invariance.
Separated-block sample splitting is valid for beta-mixing time series under stability conditions.
Kernel long-run covariance estimators are consistent under dependence and bandwidth conditions.
Fixed-role doubly robust proximal GMM has asymptotic normality when one bridge model is correct.
Fixed proximal proxy structures admit influence-function and efficiency characterizations.

body.tldr: Two predeclared valid proximal synthetic-control role assignments can identify the same ATT yet yield a nonregular conventional interval when the smaller full-pre-period ridge loss selects the reported role. The exact selected-Gaussian coverage map protects every symmetric Wald level at an exact tie and protects every local gap exactly when the two standardized ATT coordinates have equal squared selector correlations; otherwise the strict coverage-error sign is the gap sign times their squared-correlation difference. A constant-treatment one-factor Gaussian chart realizes both regimes inside a stationary square subclass of the Shi et al. model, including an open asymmetric region with coverage \(0.8857757910650707\) for a nominal \(90\%\) interval. For correction, an early selector, logarithm-squared gap, late bridge fit, post average, and future-only Bartlett standard error are uniformly selector-conditionally normal on the strengthened class with common finite-row horizon and scalar variance bounds. The same claim fails maximally on the broader pointwise-limit class, where expected conditional Kolmogorov distance can converge to one.

project_justification.gap: Published proximal synthetic-control theory predetermines donor and supplemental-proxy roles, while general post-selection results do not characterize exact ordinary symmetric-Wald coverage when a loss comparison switches between two valid proximal ATT coordinates. Pointwise horizon and limiting-variance conditions also do not support a supremum over whole triangular arrays.
project_justification.niche: The binary ridge selector admits an exact squared-correlation coverage frontier. A future-only split construction admits uniform coordinatewise studentization after imposing common finite-row horizon comparability and scalar influence-variance bounds, while singular covariance across the stacked roles remains allowed.
project_justification.fill: The paper gives the selected limit, evaluable coverage functional, all-gap if-and-only-if frontier, strict error sign, primitive open miscoverage family, and a positive/negative uniformity boundary. The corrected estimator is uniformly selector-conditionally normal on \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{stab}}(D_{\mathrm{gap}})\); a diagonal common-subclass witness proves maximal failure on \(\mathcal M(D_{\mathrm{gap}})\).

body.related_work: Shi et al. (2026) supply the fixed-role structural proximal anchor; the common-subclass proposition, not a full-class inclusion claim, transfers the present phenomena to legal stationary square panels. Leeb and Pötscher (2005) motivate local post-selection nonregularity, whereas Rakshit, Shi, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2025) address the distinct problem of adaptive selection with potentially invalid proxies. Berk et al. (2013) obtain post-selection protection by simultaneous inference, not by characterizing when an ordinary selected Wald interval is already exact. Lee et al. (2016), Leeb, Pötscher, and Ewald (2015), and Azzalini and Regoli (2012) provide related Gaussian conditioning, coverage, and symmetry tools but not the switched proximal squared-correlation frontier. Lunde (2019) and Andrews (1991) motivate separated-block dependence control and Bartlett estimation. Here those ingredients are derived for the precise future-only proximal statistic on a stabilized class, while the diagonal theorem shows why pointwise array limits alone are insufficient.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The positive theorem is uniform only over \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{stab}}(D_{\mathrm{gap}})\), whose horizon constants, threshold, and finite-row scalar variance bounds are common before the supremum is taken. It does not require nonsingularity of the stacked role covariance, but it does require fixed dimension, uniform geometric beta mixing, the declared high moment and bridge-rank margins, and future-only fitted scores. The broad class \(\mathcal M(D_{\mathrm{gap}})\) retains only arraywise limiting horizon and covariance conditions; the diagonal counterexample exploits that difference and makes the conditional approximation error maximal.
body.honest_scope: The exact coverage result concerns two predeclared square bridges, ridge penalty one, bounded root-\(n\) selector gaps, and positive marginal selector and ATT variances. The conventional interval reuses the full pre period. The corrected interval uses a fixed early fraction, a logarithm-squared gap, late bridge fitting, post residual averaging, and bandwidth exponent one fifth; its uniform theorem additionally fixes common finite-row horizon and scalar oracle-variance bounds. The Gaussian chart and diagonal witness lie in an explicit stationary constant-effect intersection with Shi et al.'s fixed-role class, but no wholesale class extension or refutation of a published fixed-role guarantee is claimed. The analysis does not cover the rectangular simplex-constrained West-German rule, estimate the local drift, restore full-pre-period efficiency, or handle more than two roles. Its actionable use is a predeclared two-candidate robustness analysis before retaining the negative GDP conclusion.
body.interpretation: For a predeclared pair of scientifically credible donor/proxy roles, conventional two-sided Wald inference is robust to local selection exactly on the squared-correlation frontier, even though the selected statistic can have nonzero mean. Off that frontier the sign formula diagnoses under- or overcoverage. If that covariance diagnostic is not defensible, the gap-split interval has a uniform justification only after the design fixes common horizon comparability and verifies finite-row scalar influence-variance margins.
